channel.title: DevPulse · Databases
channel.description: Daily databases stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Supabase acquires Turso to build on-demand databases for agents
item.description: Supabase says it is launching more than one million databases per week and wants cheap, on-demand databases with a path to production as agents build more software. That demand raises important provisioning and scaling questions for agent-oriented infrastructure.

item.title: Cloudflare Basin launches as a serverless Iceberg analytics platform
item.description: Basin is generally available with pipelines that write Apache Iceberg tables to R2, a catalog that maintains Iceberg metadata, and a distributed SQL engine for querying tables. The integrated design is relevant to engineers evaluating serverless analytics and lakehouse infrastructure.

item.title: Spanner Omni brings Spanner’s distributed, multi-model database to other clouds
item.description: Spanner Omni is generally available for on-premises data centers and other clouds, with SQL, graph, key-value, search, vector, and analytical capabilities. Teams evaluating portable database platforms can assess its breadth against their deployment needs.

item.title: Papero extracts PDF reading order, tables and formulas using geometry, not ML
item.description: Papero claims to recover PDF reading order, tables and formulas with geometric methods, running on a CPU without ML models and supporting browser and Python use. Its extraction approach may be useful when preparing documents for RAG or search.

item.title: ParadeDB responds to PlanetScale’s 8× text-search lead with optimizations
item.description: PlanetScale’s benchmark found TIN at least 8× faster than ParadeDB 0.25; ParadeDB says its follow-up used the same dataset, harness and machine types. The comparison is useful context for evaluating Postgres text-search performance claims.

item.title: Workers KV Instant uses Quicksilver for 100-times-faster p99 reads
item.description: The new KV mode uses Cloudflare’s Quicksilver global key-value store to provide immediate updates and 100-times-faster p99 reads, without waiting for TTL expiry. The design illustrates a latency trade-off for globally replicated configuration data.

item.title: DuckDB speeds string aggregations by grouping on narrow integer keys
item.description: The technique replaces repeated long strings with sorted integer keys for aggregation, then joins the strings back afterward. It is a practical query-design pattern for reducing work on variable-length values.

item.title: Backblaze Q2 drive report compares fleet failure rates and high-capacity disks
item.description: Backblaze's Q2 report reviews drive annualized failure rates, lifetime fleet records, and differences between CMR HDDs and newer high-capacity drives. Fleet-level storage reliability data can inform hardware choices, though the excerpt gives no specific results.

item.title: Jev extensions bring typed plain-English classification to DuckDB
item.description: Jev returns typed answers and probabilities, and a community DuckDB extension reportedly classifies about 1,000 rows in roughly ten seconds. The approach offers a practical alternative to LIKE filters, per-row chat calls or building a classifier for some data tasks.

item.title: FunSQL combines full SQL coverage with a compositional, data-oriented interface
item.description: FunSQL aims to support the full range of SQL queries through a compositional, data-oriented interface. Engineers generating SQL can use this framing to assess query-builder trade-offs.

item.title: DuckDB 1.5.6 fixes query-planning errors and silent integer truncation
item.description: The patch fixes optimizer pushdown and Top-N correctness issues, wrong results involving UNION ALL, and silent truncation of very long integer literals. These are concrete edge cases worth checking when upgrading embedded or analytical databases.

item.title: Cloudflare publishes BEACON data on real-world web experience
item.description: BEACON provides a view of Cloudflare's browser and network telemetry to show how people experience the web beyond high-end devices and fast connections. Engineers can use real-user data to ground performance priorities in conditions their own setups may miss.

item.title: One chef-knife brand gets 31% of recommendations from 5% of Reddit accounts
item.description: The analysis finds that one knife brand gets 31% of its recommendations from 5% of accounts and describes using a fine-tuned GLiNER model to extract product details. Its focus on measurable, recountable analysis may interest engineers building data pipelines, though the subject is consumer influence.

item.title: Datasette 1.0a41 adds OpenTelemetry and reusable modal dialogs
item.description: The release adds OpenTelemetry support and consolidates modal dialogs into a documented Web Component for plugins. The update offers concrete observability and UI integration changes for teams building data tools.

item.title: Postgres 19 beta reverts headline features as review surfaces bugs
item.description: The newsletter reports that Postgres 19 has had headline features pulled during beta and suggests AI-assisted review is surfacing bugs faster than committers can handle them. The release turbulence and review-capacity problem are relevant to teams maintaining complex software.

item.title: TIN Postgres search supports per-keystroke queries and wildcard autocomplete
item.description: A Postgres search demo uses TIN to query on every keystroke without a debounce and treats an incomplete final word as a wildcard. It illustrates how lower search latency can change interaction design, though the excerpt gives no TIN benchmark results.

item.title: DuckDB queries Hugging Face datasets directly over `hf://`
item.description: DuckDB can query CSV, JSONL, and Parquet files in Hugging Face dataset repositories through `hf://` without downloading them first. This can simplify exploratory analysis and access to ML datasets without a separate warehouse.

item.title: dbt v2 ships with a built-in DuckDB adapter
item.description: The Rust-based dbt Fusion engine ships with a built-in DuckDB adapter, alongside support for DuckLake and Iceberg catalogs and queries over dbt’s Parquet metadata. Data teams can evaluate a simpler DuckDB-based dbt setup and migration path.

item.title: Memorystore for Valkey 9.1 claims up to 3× the QPS of Redis Cluster
item.description: Google says Valkey 9.1 reaches up to three times the queries per second at microsecond latency compared with Memorystore for Redis Cluster. The release examines performance changes and developer capabilities relevant to high-throughput caching.

item.title: Postgres SELECT DISTINCT scans every matching row despite indexes
item.description: In a Postgres-backed queue workload, SELECT DISTINCT became the most expensive query because it scans every row matching the predicates, even when few unique values are needed. The explanation of the database's design trade-offs and workarounds can inform high-volume query design.

item.title: Safe-not-safe checks Postgres migrations with a browser-based parser
item.description: The tool uses libpg_query 17 compiled to WebAssembly in a browser worker, with a rule engine and no telemetry. It may help teams catch risky migration patterns, though the excerpt does not describe the rules or their coverage.
